findings.finding: The plan names close_precheck.py:64 as the ticket-type gate to widen, but the AUTHORITATIVE write-side class enforcement for closes is txn.transition_core (txn.py:260), which validates --class ONLY when ticket_type=='bug' and otherwise folds close_class onto the edge (txn.py:287) with no validation. Widening the disposition path to non-bug tickets without extending transition_core's guard means (a) a non-bug ticket can be closed with an unvalidated/bogus class, and (b) the not_a_bug/escalated bug-only refusal (AC2) has no enforcement point on the non-bug path.
scenarios: Operator runs `transition <task-id> in_progress closed --class not_a_bug` — should be refused (bug-only class on a task) but transition_core does not validate non-bug class

evidence: close_precheck.py:472 `if force_close: return None` — the completion precheck (where disposition logic lives) is bypassed on force and when the gate is disabled
close_precheck.py:464 gate_enabled check — the whole precheck is skipped when the gate is off

close_class is persisted in transition_core (txn.py:287) independent of the gate
findings.finding: The plan requires obsolete/wontfix to demand a close_reason with 'refusal when missing' (Fix.3, AC3) and superseded/duplicate to demand a live replacement, but does not state WHERE these refusals are enforced relative to the write lock and --force. The existing disposition/precheck logic (_completion_precheck) returns early on force_close (close_precheck.py:472) and runs outside the write lock, while close_class is persisted authoritatively in transition_core. Without naming the enforcement point, a required-reason check placed only in the completion-gate precheck would be silently skipped when the gate is off or on --force, letting an obsolete close persist with no reason.
scenarios: Completion gate disabled in a repo: an obsolete close with no reason persists because the reason-required check lived only in the gated precheck
Operator uses --force: the reason requirement is skipped
